subject: chemistry
title: Formulae, equations and the mole
key_idea: Ionic formulae balance the charges of the ions. Equations must balance atoms and charge, with state symbols. The mole counts particles: one mole is 6.02 × 10²³ of them, and its mass in grams is the molar mass.

blocks.text: An ionic formula shows the simplest ratio of ions, with total positive charge equal to total negative charge. This section covers how to predict ion charges and combine them.
Predicting a charge from the Periodic Table

items.text: Aluminium sulfate contains Al³⁺ and SO₄²⁻.
Two Al³⁺ give +6. Three SO₄²⁻ give −6.
Put a compound ion in brackets when you need more than one: Al₂(SO₄)₃.

items: The group predicts the charge on a simple ion.
Total positive charge equals total negative charge.
Use brackets around a compound ion when there is more than one.

blocks.text: An equation must have the same atoms and the same total charge on each side. This section covers full equations, ionic equations and state symbols.

items.meaning: (s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas, (aq) dissolved in water.
An ion that is in the mixture but does not change during the reaction.
An equation showing only the particles that react.

items.lead: Split the aqueous ionic compounds into ions.

items.text: K⁺ and NO₃⁻ appear unchanged on both sides.

items: Only aqueous ionic compounds and strong acids are split into ions. Solids, liquids and gases stay whole.
Check two things: atoms balance, and total charge is the same on both sides.
For an unfamiliar reaction, use the reactants and products you are given, then balance.
Never change a formula to balance an equation. Change only the number in front.
Balance atoms and charge.
State symbols are part of the answer.
An ionic equation leaves out the spectator ions.

sections.heading: The mole, the Avogadro constant and molar mass

blocks.text: Atoms are too small to count one by one, so chemists count them in moles. This section covers the mole and how it links mass and numbers of particles.

items.meaning: A quantity measured in moles, written n.
The unit of amount of substance. One mole contains 6.02 × 10²³ particles.
The number of particles per mole: 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
The mass of one mole of a substance, in g mol⁻¹. It has the same number as the relative formula mass.

items: Always say which particle you mean: a mole of O atoms is not a mole of O₂ molecules.
The particles can be atoms, molecules, ions, electrons or formula units.
Amount is written with the formula: amount of NaCl, amount of O₂.
Molar mass of H₂O = 2 × 1.0 + 16.0 = 18.0 g mol⁻¹.

items.text: Each H₂O has 3 atoms, so there are 9.03 × 10²³ atoms.

diagram.alt: A calculation of the number of water molecules in a given mass of water.
diagram.question: How many molecules are in {m} g of water (molar mass 18.0 g mol⁻¹)? Give the answer as a multiple of 10²³.

items: One mole is 6.02 × 10²³ particles.
n = m ÷ M links mass to amount.
Multiply moles by the Avogadro constant to count particles.

checks.q: Write the formula of aluminium nitrate and of ammonium carbonate.
Write the ionic equation, with state symbols, for silver nitrate solution reacting with sodium chloride solution to form a precipitate of silver chloride.
checks.a: Ag⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) → AgCl(s). Na⁺ and NO₃⁻ are spectator ions.

checks.q: Calculate the number of oxygen atoms in 1.60 g of O₂. (Molar mass of O₂ = 32.0 g mol⁻¹; L = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.)
checks.a: n(O₂) = 1.60 ÷ 32.0 = 0.0500 mol. Molecules = 0.0500 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 3.01 × 10²². Each molecule has 2 atoms, so 6.02 × 10²² atoms.

items: Charges on ions other than the group-based ones and the recall list are given to you in the question.
'Nitrate' and 'sulfate' always mean NO₃⁻ and SO₄²⁻.
Either the carbon-12 definition or the Avogadro-constant definition of the mole is accepted.
The Avogadro constant may be written Nₐ, with the same value, 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
Molar gas volume is the gas volume per mole, in dm³ mol⁻¹. Its value at room temperature and pressure is on the data sheet.
The Avogadro constant is written L, with the value 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹, and is used in calculations.
Write balanced full equations and ionic equations for reactions, always with state symbols.
The mole applies to electrons, atoms, molecules, ions, formulae and equations.
Concentration of a solution is measured in mol dm⁻³. Calculate it from concentration, volume and amount: n = c × V.
Calculate with mass, relative molecular mass (Mᵣ) and amount in moles.
You do not need to recall the value of the Avogadro constant.
Oxidation numbers shown by a Roman numeral give the charge: iron(III) oxide contains Fe³⁺, so its formula is Fe₂O₃.
Also recall hydrogencarbonate, HCO₃⁻, and phosphate, PO₄³⁻.
An ionic equation must not include spectator ions.
Use state symbols appropriately in every equation.
